title: Nan waveform investigation — seed sensitivity + microburst notes
content:
Summary:
A streak of intermittent NaNs shows up during FP8-enabled inference for a trimmed LLM (approx 7B transformer). Failures are short-lived (a few batches) and then the model recovers. Appears correlated with certain request shapes (short prompt followed by long sampling), and has higher incidence on A100-80GB configs when CUDA graph + continuous-batching is enabled. Repro is flaky but I have a >1% hit rate on nightly stress runs.

Symptoms observed:
- Outputs: token logits collapse to all NaN for 1-3 generated steps, then return to normal.
- Logs: runtime prints 'nan in kv cache' in one debug hook, and later 'inf in softmax' in another.
- No GPU OOM. No host OOM.
- Happens only when running with FP8 quantization profile applied. BF16/FP16 runs show no NaNs.
- Slightly more frequent when running sequences with many short prefix tokens then long sampling windows (>512 gen steps).

Timeline (quick):
- 2025-02-03: First reported by SE investigating a customer workload (dedicated cluster).
- 2025-02-04: Reproduced locally on A100 with CUDA graph enabled, 4 shot prompts.
- 2025-02-06: Bisect suggested correlation with latest cuBLAS update (but couldn't fully repro on older driver).
- 2025-02-10: Micro-benchmark shows seed-dependent burst behavior.

Commands / repro attempts (most relevant):
- baseline FP32 run (no quant):
  python infer_cli.py --model gptx-7b --dtype float32 --prompt-file samples/p1.txt --max-tokens 256 --batch 1

- fp8 run that often fails (example):
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infer_cli.py --model gptx-7b --dtype fp8 --quant-config configs/fp8-compact.yaml --prompt-file samples/p1.txt --max-tokens 1024 --batch 1 --use-cuda-graphs --continuous-batching

- reduced experiment (deterministic seeds):
  PYTORCH_SEED=1234 TORCH_USE_DISTRIBUTED=0 python tools/repro_microburst.py --model gptx-7b --dtype fp8 --steps 200 --prompt-shape "short->long"

Snippet of failing log (copied raw):
  [2025-02-04T18:22:41Z] runtime DEBUG kv_cache: layer 10 write idx 34 -> values contain NaN(s)
  [2025-02-04T18:22:41Z] runtime WARN attention: softmax produced INF at head 3 (sum=Inf)
  [2025-02-04T18:22:42Z] runtime ERROR sample_loop: sample returned NaN logits, aborting step

Quick stack guess: softmax receives extremely large logits (maybe due to denormals, uninitialized kv values, or quant dequant mis-scaling). Could also be tiny rounding errors cascading in FP8 GEMM path.

What I've tried so far (and results):
- Re-run same script with --no-cuda-graphs: failure rate dropped ~60% but still occurs.
- Turn off continuous batching: slight improvement. Hypothesis: batching + graph causes subtle uninitialized buffer reuse.
- Set torch.backends.cudnn.enabled = False: no effect.
- Run on H100 (same driver): lower frequency but still non-zero.
- Force KV cache zeroing before writes (memset): reduced occurrence in microbench but not eliminated; suggests transient write races or precision blow-ups rather than stale memory entirely.
- Compare fp8 quantization table variants: two profiles (scale per-tensor vs per-channel) — per-channel reduced frequency.
- Increase softmax clipping (clip logits to +/- 100): mitigates symptom but masks root cause.
- Run with denormal flushing (FTZ/DAZ) on CPU side: not applicable to GPU kernels.
- Insert post-GEMM sanity clamp for NaN/INF to detect where NaNs first appear; first NaNs observed right after attention value projection GEMM (V * W_v) for some batches.

Repro matrix (approx):
- Dtype: FP32 (0% fails), BF16 (0%), FP16 (0%), FP8 (1–3% fail depending on env)
- Device: A100-80GB (2–3%), H100 (0.5–1%)
- CUDA graphs: on (higher), off (lower)
- Continuous-batching: on (higher), off (lower)
- Quant profile: per-channel (lower), per-tensor (higher)
- Batch size: 1 (more visible), >1 (less visible but still exists)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quant dequant scaling edge-case: very small scales cause overflow after dequant in some kernels -> INF on softmax input. Explains crop to FP8 only. Per-channel profile reduces because scales are more accurate.
2) CUDA-graph + reuse bug: when graphs re-use buffer addresses, small FP8 deltas may leave residues leading to NaN in subsequent runs. Memset reduced incidence.
3) Random seed sensitivity: RNG sequence interacts with rounding to produce rare pathological activations. Matches seed-dependency observed.
4) cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel numerical issue on certain driver combos causing instability on FP8 path.

Minimal repro recipe (best effort):
1) Use A100 machine, driver >= 535.x, cuBLAS recent.
2) Checkout branch: runtime/fp8-experiments-local (PR #823).
3) Run: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/repro_microburst.py --model gptx-7b --dtype fp8 --steps 300 --prompt-shape "short->long" --seed 8675309 --use-cuda-graphs --continuous-batching
4) If failure doesn't show, toggle seed and repeat ~20x.

Quick experiments log (abridged):
- seed 8675309: pass
- seed 42: fail at step 74 (NaN in V projection)
- seed 314159: pass
- seed 999983: fail at step 12 (softmax INF)
- run w/ per-channel quant: seeds 42 and 999983 both passed

Debugging notes for next runs (actionable):
- Add finer-grained instrumentation around V GEMM outputs: dump min/max/std and any NaN/Inf masks for failing batches only. Keep telemetry lightweight (sample only ~1/1000 batches).
- Add explicit dequant scaling sanity checks (scale within [1e-5, 1e5]) before GEMM, log anomalies.
- Try building with cublasLT disabled to see if different GEMM paths change frequency.
- Reproduce with ASAN/UBSAN-like GPU memory checks if feasible (cuda-memcheck?).
- Try turning on deterministic cudnn and set TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1? (investigate platform flags for deterministic GPU kernels).
- Short-term mitigation: prefer per-channel FP8 quant profiles for customer workloads; add softmax clamping as a safety net in runtime.

Notes and stray thoughts:
- The term 'waveform' is my mental model: NaNs appear in short bursts that look like microbursts in telemetry. Could be due to rare input patterns causing exponent spikes in logits.
- Customer impact: intermittent failures are annoying but often transient; still need root cause for SLA and audit.
- Communication: tell CS that we can recommend per-channel FP8 or temporary fallback to BF16 for critical flows.

Next steps (short):
- Instrument V GEMM and softmax as above; run 1000 seed sweep overnight on both A100 and H100 (assign to nightly slot).
- Try disabling CUDA graphs in dedicated clusters as temporary mitigation; monitor customer error rate.
- Pair with runtime + infra to test different cuBLAS versions.

If you pick this up, start by re-running repro_microburst.py with seed=42 and the per-channel vs per-tensor quant configs and attach logs to INF-1724.

-- Jordan
